Current ideation present; intent absent; plan absent; access reviewed true. Disposition: Outpatient care with a psychiatric consultation in three days and close follow-up. C-SSRS screen: wish to be dead on several days in the past month; no active thoughts of suicide, intent, plan, preparation or past attempt. Risk factors reviewed: severe depression, an older man, insomnia, loss of work and income, isolation, and sustained persecution. Means counseling: there is no firearm in the home and he will not acquire one; medicines will be dispensed in limited supplies and kept in a locked box. A written safety plan was made with him, with warning signs, coping steps, people and places for distraction, and crisis numbers; the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) was saved in his phone. Safety is reviewed at every visit.

text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Evaluation: PHQ-9, GAD-7, AUDIT-C and a cognitive screen (MoCA); blood count, metabolic panel, calcium, TSH, vitamin B12, folate, morning testosterone and hemoglobin A1c, with HIV and syphilis tests, to exclude medical causes; a review of medicines; and a sleep apnea screen
  • Urgent psychiatric consultation in three days to confirm the diagnosis with a structured interview, screen for bipolar disorder, judge suicide risk and the level of care, and advise on psychotherapy, medicines, and when ECT or other treatments would be indicated
  • Safety: structured suicide-risk assessment, a written safety plan, no firearm in the home, medicines dispensed in limited supplies and kept locked, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and a safety review at every visit
  • Trust and equity: explain who can see his record and how it is protected; a therapist of his choosing, including a Black clinician if he wishes; treat discrimination and persecution as real stressors and record his account of surveillance as realistic; a social worker for help with income and costs; guard against the documented under-treatment of depression in Black patients by measuring response at every visit
  • Treatment: behavioral activation weekly with a psychologist for about sixteen sessions, then CBT if needed; sertraline 50 mg, raised to 100 mg at two weeks and to 200 mg by eight weeks as tolerated; PHQ-9 at every visit with response defined as a 50 percent fall and remission as a score below 5; sodium at about six weeks; switch to an SNRI if the PHQ-9 falls by less than a quarter after an adequate trial, and consider augmentation, ECT, rTMS or esketamine if a second adequate trial brings only a partial response; watch for hypomania after starting an antidepressant
  • Switch to venlafaxine extended-release by cross-taper: venlafaxine 75 mg for a week while sertraline is halved, then 150 mg for three weeks and 225 mg; blood pressure at every visit; 30-day supplies because venlafaxine is more dangerous in overdose
  • Treatment-resistant depression: aripiprazole 2 mg, raised to 5 mg at two weeks, with weight at four, eight and twelve weeks, A1c and lipids at baseline and twelve weeks, and an abnormal involuntary movement examination at baseline and six months; an informed consent discussion about ECT (general anesthesia with a muscle relaxant, right unilateral ultrabrief pulse, two or three treatments a week in a defined course, cognitive testing before and during the course, and the right to stop at any time), with rTMS and esketamine as alternatives; ECT not started now and offered if augmentation fails or if he becomes unable to eat or drink, psychotic or acutely suicidal
  • Acute bronchitis: no antibiotic and no chest X-ray with normal vital signs and a normal chest examination; honey, warm drinks and steam; plain guaifenesin if needed; no dextromethorphan, which with venlafaxine can cause serotonin syndrome, and no pseudoephedrine or phenylephrine, which raise blood pressure further on venlafaxine; check labels of combination cold remedies; return for fever, breathlessness, chest pain or a cough lasting more than three weeks
  • Prevention: stool FIT kit for colorectal screening; the earlier prostate surgery records obtained before any decision on PSA testing; a ten-year cardiovascular risk of about 9 percent discussed, with his choice of diet and activity first and a statin to be reconsidered in a year; hepatitis B and C screening; influenza, PCV20 and the first recombinant zoster dose today, the second zoster dose in two to six months

resource.title: Paul Robeson synthetic care plan
resource.description: Recognize and treat recurrent severe major depression in a 58-year-old Black singer, actor and activist under sustained political persecution, as the APA 1950 and VA/DoD 1953 guidelines and the CMID depression monograph advise: PHQ-9 and GAD-7, a structured diagnostic interview, bipolar screening with the MDQ before an antidepressant, a structured suicide-risk assessment with a safety plan, means counseling and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and tests to exclude medical causes; treating realistic fears of surveillance as realistic rather than as paranoia, and attending to the documented racial disparities in the diagnosis of depression, its treatment and access to ECT; behavioral activation with measurement-based care; adequate trials of an SSRI (sertraline to 200 mg) and an SNRI (venlafaxine to 225 mg), then aripiprazole augmentation for treatment-resistant depression with metabolic monitoring; and an informed consent discussion about modern ECT (general anesthesia, right unilateral ultrabrief pulse, a defined course with cognitive testing) and its alternatives (rTMS and esketamine), decided against for now and kept available. The modern record contrasts careful, consented, measured modern ECT with what is documented about the many treatments he received years later, without asserting the disputed allegations about his care. It is a teaching case, not a claim about his real illness or care.
